population.name: reactive_tool_assisted_recovery_v7
population.description: Implements a reactive error recovery mechanism leveraging dynamically generated tools to handle LLM failures. Introduces a 'multi-attempt' strategy with diverse prompt variations.
population.approach: When the LLM returns an error (e.g., timeout, invalid response format), the system generates a specialized tool using the LLM itself. This tool is designed to either reformat the LLM's prompt, simplify the request, or query an alternative data source to fulfill the original user request. Employs a multi-attempt approach with each attempt using a different generated tool or prompt variation. The system also includes a mechanism to learn from past errors and prioritize successful recovery tools for future similar errors. Incorporates 'with'-statement based resource management to ensure proper tool cleanup.

population.name: cwmai_evolutionary_dependency_management_v4_performance
population.description: This version of the evolutionary dependency management system is optimized for performance by leveraging a combination of caching, parallel processing, knowledge retrieval for common dependency patterns, and on-demand tool generation for specialized dependency resolution. It prioritizes speed without sacrificing solution quality, aiming for near real-time dependency resolution for large projects.

approach.initialization: Start with a diverse population of dependency graphs generated using a combination of existing project dependency information, curated knowledge base of common patterns, and randomly generated structures. Utilize a Bloom filter to quickly identify and filter out redundant or already-explored dependency configurations.
approach.fitness_evaluation: The fitness function is modified to heavily prioritize speed. It evaluates dependency graphs based on several factors: (1) Resolution Time: The time taken to resolve all dependencies; (2) Graph Complexity: Number of dependencies and nodes; (3) Security Vulnerabilities: Number of known vulnerabilities in the chosen versions; (4) License Compatibility: Cost of licenses required based on the dependency versions.  A weighted sum of these factors determines fitness.  Caching of previously calculated fitness values is employed to avoid redundant computations.
approach.selection: Tournament selection is used due to its speed and efficiency.  Multiple tournaments are run in parallel to further improve performance. Elitism is implemented to ensure the best solutions are always carried forward.
approach.crossover: A specialized crossover operator combines subgraphs from parent dependency graphs, prioritizing subgraphs that have high fitness scores and are compatible with each other. The knowledge retrieval component is used to guide the crossover process by suggesting potentially compatible subgraphs from the knowledge base.
approach.mutation: Mutation operators include adding new dependencies, removing existing dependencies, and changing dependency versions. A dynamic mutation rate is used, with higher mutation rates early in the process to explore the solution space more broadly, and lower mutation rates later to refine the solutions.  Mutation events are also influenced by the knowledge retrieval service to increase the probability of valid dependency relationships.
approach.termination: The algorithm terminates when a satisfactory solution (below a predefined fitness threshold for 'resolution time') is found, or after a maximum number of generations. Early stopping is also implemented based on the stagnation of the best fitness score.
approach.knowledge_retrieval: A knowledge retrieval system stores common dependency patterns, version compatibility information, and known security vulnerabilities. This system is continuously updated with new data.  The evolutionary algorithm queries this knowledge base to inform initialization, crossover, mutation, and fitness evaluation.
approach.tool_generation: A tool generation service can generate specialized dependency resolution tools on-demand. This is useful for resolving complex dependencies that are not easily handled by the standard evolutionary algorithm. The tool generation service uses a combination of code templates and configuration files to create the tools.
approach.parallelization: Significant parallelization is implemented using multiprocessing or threading libraries in Python. The fitness evaluation, selection, crossover, and mutation operations are all parallelized to speed up the evolutionary process.

metrics.resolution_time: Average time taken to resolve dependencies (target: sub-second resolution for most projects).
metrics.graph_complexity: Number of dependencies and nodes in the final dependency graph (lower is better).
metrics.security_vulnerabilities: Number of known security vulnerabilities in the chosen dependency versions (zero is ideal).
metrics.license_compatibility_cost: The monetary or administrative cost associated with the licenses of the selected dependencies (lower is better).
metrics.solution_quality: Overall fitness score of the best solution.
metrics.knowledge_retrieval_hit_rate: Percentage of times the knowledge retrieval system provides useful information.
metrics.tool_generation_frequency: Number of times the tool generation service is used.

population.name: Reactive Evolutionary Dependency Guardian
population.description: A system that proactively manages dependencies and automatically generates fixes for dependency-related errors. It leverages CI/CD pipeline monitoring, reactive error detection via logging analysis, and evolutionary dependency updates informed by tool-generated suggestions and historical build data. This allows for faster recovery from dependency-related failures and continuous improvement of dependency configurations.
population.approach: The system monitors CI/CD pipelines for build failures and runtime exceptions linked to dependency issues. When such an error occurs, it triggers a tool generation service to suggest potential fixes (e.g., dependency version downgrades, code modifications, or workarounds). The suggestions are then ranked based on historical CI/CD performance data and applied to a staging environment. Successful builds in the staging environment trigger an automatic pull request to the main branch, incorporating the fix. Simultaneously, an evolutionary algorithm refines the dependency configuration over time, learning from the success and failure of past build attempts and integrating tool-generated insights to optimize for stability, performance, and security. The system uses reactive triggers based on log analysis and proactive dependency health checks to identify potential issues before they impact production.
metrics: Mean Time To Recovery (MTTR) for dependency-related failures
Number of dependency-related build failures per sprint
Percentage of automatically resolved dependency issues
Dependency stability score (based on CI/CD build success rate)
Number of critical vulnerabilities introduced by dependency changes
integration_points: CI/CD pipeline (monitoring build status and triggering fixes)
Logging service (reactive error detection and analysis)
Tool generation service (suggesting fixes for dependency issues)
Version control system (creating and managing pull requests)
Dependency management tool (e.g., Maven, npm, pip - for dependency resolution and updates)
Monitoring system (tracking dependency health and performance)
Alerting system (notifying developers of critical issues)
Security vulnerability scanner (integrating with dependency management)
Build system (e.g., Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions)

population.name: Proactive Recovery Orchestrator (v8)
population.description: An advanced recovery system leveraging proactive anomaly detection, LLM-powered diagnosis, and automated remediation workflows orchestrated through a central engine. It incorporates a factuality checker to ensure the accuracy of LLM-generated remediation steps and continuous monitoring to dynamically adjust recovery strategies.
population.approach: The Proactive Recovery Orchestrator employs a multi-stage approach: 1. **Proactive Anomaly Detection:** Utilizes time-series analysis and machine learning models (trained on historical system data and operational metrics) to predict potential failures *before* they fully manifest. 2. **LLM-Driven Diagnosis:** When an anomaly is detected, an LLM, specifically trained on system logs, incident reports, and documentation, is triggered. It analyzes the anomaly and generates a preliminary diagnosis, including potential root causes and suggested remediation steps. 3. **Factuality Check & Refinement:** The LLM's suggested remediation steps are passed through a factuality checker. This component cross-references the LLM's output with authoritative sources (e.g., configuration management databases, vendor documentation, known issue databases) to verify the accuracy and applicability of the proposed actions. In case of discrepancies, the LLM is prompted to refine its suggestions based on the factual data. 4. **Automated Remediation Workflow:** A workflow engine orchestrates the execution of the factuality-validated remediation steps. This involves interacting with various tools and systems (e.g., configuration management, orchestration platforms, ticketing systems) through pre-defined workflows or dynamically generated scripts. 5. **Continuous Monitoring & Adaptation:** The system continuously monitors the impact of the remediation actions. If the anomaly persists or new issues arise, the system re-engages the LLM for further diagnosis and adjustment of the remediation plan. A feedback loop incorporates monitoring data into the anomaly detection models to improve future predictions and the LLM's training dataset for more accurate diagnoses.
metrics: Accuracy of LLM diagnosis (compared to human expert)
Percentage of remediation steps validated by factuality checker
Reduction in human intervention required for incident resolution
Number of false positives from anomaly detection
Cost savings due to automated recovery

integration_points.integration:anomaly_detection: Connects to time-series databases and monitoring systems to ingest system metrics and logs for proactive anomaly detection. Uses APIs and streaming data interfaces.
integration_points.integration:llm_inference_engine: Leverages a pre-trained and fine-tuned LLM accessible via API for diagnosis and remediation suggestion generation. Supports configurable prompting and model versioning.
integration_points.integration:factuality_checker: Connects to CMDBs, vendor documentation repositories, and other authoritative data sources to validate the LLM's outputs. Implements APIs for data retrieval and comparison.
integration_points.integration:workflow_engine: Orchestrates the execution of remediation steps using a workflow engine that supports branching, error handling, and integration with various IT tools. Integrates via APIs and message queues.
integration_points.integration:monitoring: Continuously monitors system health and performance after remediation, providing feedback to the anomaly detection models and LLM. Uses agents, APIs, and streaming data.
integration_points.integration:ticketing_system: Automatically creates and updates incident tickets based on detected anomalies and remediation actions. Integrates via APIs.
integration_points.integration:configuration_management: Reads and updates system configurations to ensure consistent and accurate remediation. Integrates via APIs and configuration management protocols (e.g., Ansible, Puppet).
integration_points.integration:security_information_and_eve: Alerts SIEM systems on detected anomalies and executed remediation actions. Sends logs and alerts via SIEM-compatible formats.
integration_points.integration:logging: Logs all actions performed by the orchestrator, including anomaly detections, LLM diagnoses, factuality checks, and remediation steps. Provides a comprehensive audit trail for incident analysis.
integration_points.integration:identity_and_access_manageme: Integrates with IAM systems to ensure authorized access to system resources for remediation actions.  Uses API-based authentication and authorization.

population.name: CWMAI_EvolutionaryDependencyManagement_v4
population.description: An AI-powered system that proactively manages dependencies in a software project, minimizing risks and promoting stability through continuous evolution and automated governance. It extends traditional dependency management by incorporating predictive risk assessment, automated remediation suggestions, and policy enforcement driven by machine learning. Integrates deeply with CI/CD pipelines and monitoring systems for real-time insights and proactive intervention.

approach.core_engine: CWMAIEvolutionaryDependencyManagement (hybrid of v3 and v3_v3 logic)
approach.risk_prediction: Employs machine learning models trained on historical dependency data, vulnerability databases, and project-specific code patterns to predict potential dependency-related risks (e.g., security vulnerabilities, compatibility issues, license violations). The models are continuously retrained based on new data and feedback loops.
approach.automated_remediation: Suggests automated remediation strategies, such as dependency upgrades, alternative dependency recommendations, or code refactoring, based on the predicted risks and defined policies. These suggestions are prioritized based on impact and feasibility.
approach.policy_enforcement: Enforces dependency management policies defined by the organization, such as allowed dependency versions, license requirements, and security compliance rules. Violations are automatically detected and flagged, triggering remediation actions or CI/CD pipeline failures.
approach.evolutionary_adaptation: Continuously adapts its risk assessment and remediation strategies based on the evolving dependency landscape and project-specific context. This is achieved through reinforcement learning and Bayesian optimization, ensuring that the system remains effective over time.
approach.human_in_the-loop: Provides a user-friendly interface for developers and security engineers to review and approve automated remediation suggestions, adjust policies, and provide feedback on the system's performance. This ensures that the system remains aligned with the organization's goals and values.

metrics.dependency_risk_score: A composite score that quantifies the overall risk associated with the project's dependencies, taking into account vulnerability severity, license compliance, compatibility issues, and other factors.
metrics.mean_time_to_remediate: The average time it takes to resolve dependency-related issues, such as security vulnerabilities or compatibility conflicts.
metrics.policy_compliance_rate: The percentage of dependencies that comply with the organization's dependency management policies.
metrics.vulnerability_detection_rate: The percentage of known vulnerabilities that are detected by the system before they are exploited.
metrics.remediation_acceptance_rate: The percentage of automated remediation suggestions that are accepted by developers or security engineers.
metrics.cost_avoidance: Estimated cost savings resulting from reduced vulnerability exploits and faster issue resolution.

integration_points.ci_cd_pipelines: Integrates with CI/CD pipelines to automatically scan dependencies, enforce policies, and trigger remediation actions during the build and deployment process. This ensures that only compliant and secure dependencies are deployed to production.
integration_points.code_repositories: Connects to code repositories (e.g., GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket) to analyze dependency graphs, track dependency usage, and identify potential risks.
integration_points.vulnerability_databases: Integrates with vulnerability databases (e.g., NIST National Vulnerability Database, Snyk) to stay up-to-date on the latest security threats and vulnerabilities.
integration_points.package_managers: Supports various package managers (e.g., npm, pip, Maven, Gradle) to automatically manage dependencies and resolve conflicts.
integration_points.monitoring_systems: Integrates with monitoring systems to track dependency-related performance issues and security incidents in real-time. Alerts are triggered when suspicious activity is detected.
integration_points.slack_notifications: Provides real-time notifications to developers and security engineers about dependency-related risks, policy violations, and remediation suggestions via Slack or other communication channels.
integration_points.security_information_and_event_managemen: Integrates with SIEM systems to provide a consolidated view of dependency security risks and incidents across the organization.
